item.content:encoded:
A unilateral ‘energy truce’? Day 1693 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-16

Despite a slowdown in the pace of Ukrainian counterattacks in the Lyman sector, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) are not giving up on their attempts to dislodge the enemy from most of the remaining positions on the western bank of the Zherebets River.Ukrainian troops have managed to expand the area under their control in the northern part of Zarichne and advance towards the town centre. The defenders have also managed to regain control of most of the large forest complex north of Rai-Oleksandrivka. Fighting for its central streets is currently taking place, though a vast grey zone still persists there. According to unconfirmed reports from Russian sources, the Ukrainians have managed to cross the Donets–Donbas Canal in small groups.

item.title: [19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland] Saxony-Anhalt: AfD and BSW demand an end to aid for Ukraine
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Saxony-Anhalt: AfD and BSW demand an end to aid for Ukraine

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-16

At a special session on 14 October, the parliament of Saxony-Anhalt adopted a joint resolution submitted by the Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), entitled ‘Peace talks instead of expanding the war in Ukraine’. The AfD (39 MPs) and BSW (5) hold a majority in the 83-seat state parliament (Landtag) but have not formed a formal coalition. In the resolution, the two parliamentary groups call for an immediate ceasefire and the start of negotiations with Russia, alongside the normalisation of economic relations and the immediate lifting of sanctions. Its authors argue that “the energy and economic war being waged against Russia is inflicting enormous losses on German industry, businesses, trade and our citizens”. The AfD and BSW demand a halt to arms deliveries and all financial assistance to Ukraine, with the exception of humanitarian aid. In the longer term, they also want Ukraine to be granted neutral status.

The resolution brings together earlier demands by the AfD and BSW to end German support for Ukraine. However, it also marks the first attempt to advance these demands through the Bundesrat, Germany’s upper house. In practice, the resolution would only be submitted to the Bundesrat by a new AfD-led state government.

item.title: [19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland] War of nerves: Ukraine needs funding, EU demands reforms
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
War of nerves: Ukraine needs funding, EU demands reforms

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-16

For several weeks, the Ukrainian authorities have been highlighting acute liquidity problems. President Volodymyr Zelensky estimated that an additional $27 billion would be needed for defence by the end of this year, while Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi stressed that the government must secure $29.5 billion from international partners this year to finance civilian budget expenditure, of which more than $3 billion has already been received. Kyiv has therefore called on the EU to identify new support mechanisms and release some of the funding earmarked for 2027 before the end of this year.

The European Commission has indicated that Ukraine could receive a further €32.5 billion from the EU in 2026 – €17.1 billion in budget support conditional on reforms and €15.4 billion in guaranteed funding for military needs. This would cover part of the country’s financing requirements.

The budget shortfall most likely stems from defence spending at a faster rate than planned in the spring and summer, as well as a decline in tax revenues caused by intensified Russian strikes. An equally important factor, however, is the authorities’ lack of political will to implement key reforms concerning the rule of law and the fight against corruption, which has led to the suspension of further tranches of EU assistance.
